points.title: 音乐启蒙
points.description: 贝多芬1770年出生于德国波恩，他的祖父是波恩宫廷乐长，父亲是宫廷歌手。尽管家庭环境并不富裕，但贝多芬从小就展现出非凡的音乐天赋。在波恩，他接受了早期音乐教育，师从宫廷管风琴师克里斯蒂安·戈特洛布·内费。1787年，他首次前往维也纳，希望跟随莫扎特学习，但因母亲病重而返回。在波恩的最后几年，他创作了早期作品，包括《选帝侯奏鸣曲》和《三个钢琴四重奏》，这些作品已经显示出他独特的音乐风格和对传统形式的突破。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Bonn in 1770, Beethoven came from a musical family. His grandfather was Kapellmeister at the Bonn court, and his father was a court singer. Despite financial difficulties, Beethoven showed exceptional musical talent from an early age. In Bonn, he received his early musical education under court organist Christian Gottlob Neefe. In 1787, he first traveled to Vienna hoping to study with Mozart but had to return due to his mother's illness. During his final years in Bonn, he composed early works including the 'Electoral Sonatas' and 'Three Piano Quartets,' which already showed his unique musical style and departure from traditional forms.

points.title: 崭露头角
points.description: 1792年，贝多芬第二次前往维也纳，师从海顿学习作曲，并很快在维也纳的音乐界崭露头角。他作为钢琴演奏家的才华令人惊叹，即兴演奏尤其出色。这一时期，他创作了《第一交响曲》、《第一钢琴协奏曲》和《第一钢琴奏鸣曲》等重要作品。1796年，他开始注意到听力逐渐下降，这对音乐家来说是致命的打击。尽管面临这一困境，贝多芬在维也纳迅速建立起声誉，成为维也纳最杰出的钢琴家和作曲家之一。1799年，他出版了《八首变奏曲》，献给他的学生，伯爵夫人布伦瑞克。
points.descriptionEn: In 1792, Beethoven traveled to Vienna for the second time, studying composition with Haydn, and quickly made a name for himself in Vienna's musical circles. His talent as a pianist was astonishing, particularly his improvisations. During this period, he composed important works including his 'First Symphony,' 'First Piano Concerto,' and 'First Piano Sonata.' In 1796, he began noticing his gradually declining hearing, a devastating blow for a musician. Despite this challenge, Beethoven rapidly built his reputation in Vienna, becoming one of the city's most distinguished pianists and composers. In 1799, he published 'Eight Variations,' dedicated to his student, Countess Brunsvik.

points.title: 创作巅峰
points.description: 这是贝多芬创作生涯中最辉煌的时期。尽管听力持续恶化，他创作了《第三交响曲（英雄）》、《第五交响曲》、《第六交响曲（田园）》、《第九交响曲》等不朽杰作。1808年，他完成了《第五钢琴协奏曲（皇帝）》，这是他最著名的钢琴协奏曲之一。1809年，拿破仑军队占领维也纳，贝多芬被迫躲藏，但继续创作。1812年，他写下了著名的《致永恒的爱人》信件，表达了他对一位神秘女性的炽热情感。这一时期，贝多芬的音乐风格发生了重大转变，从古典主义转向更加个人化、情感化的表达，为浪漫主义音乐开辟了道路。
points.descriptionEn: This was the most glorious period of Beethoven's creative career. Despite his continued hearing loss, he composed immortal masterpieces including his 'Third Symphony (Heroic),' 'Fifth Symphony,' 'Sixth Symphony (Pastoral),' and 'Ninth Symphony.' In 1808, he completed his 'Fifth Piano Concerto (Emperor),' one of his most famous piano concertos. In 1809, Napoleon's army occupied Vienna, forcing Beethoven to take refuge while continuing to compose. In 1812, he wrote the famous 'Letter to the Immortal Beloved,' expressing his passionate feelings for a mysterious woman. During this period, Beethoven's musical style underwent a significant transformation, shifting from classicism toward more personal and emotional expression, paving the way for Romantic music.

points.title: 晚年困境
points.description: 1815年，贝多芬的兄弟卡尔的去世引发了一场长达五年的监护权争夺战，贝多芬最终获得了侄子的监护权，但这一经历给他带来了巨大的精神压力。此时，他的听力已经完全丧失，无法再进行公开演出或指挥。然而，贝多芬并没有停止创作，反而进入了更加深刻的创作阶段。1818年，他开始使用'谈话册'与人交流。这一时期，他创作了《庄严弥撒》和《第十七弦乐四重奏》等重要作品。尽管面临个人困境和身体残疾，贝多芬的音乐创作达到了新的深度，展现出人类精神面对逆境时的坚韧与超越。
points.descriptionEn: In 1815, the death of Beethoven's brother Karl sparked a five-year custody battle for his nephew, which Beethoven eventually won but at great emotional cost. By this time, his hearing had completely failed, preventing him from performing publicly or conducting. However, Beethoven did not stop composing; instead, he entered an even more profound creative phase. In 1818, he began using 'conversation books' to communicate. During this period, he composed important works including the 'Missa Solemnis' and 'String Quartet No. 17.' Despite personal struggles and physical disability, Beethoven's musical composition reached new depths, demonstrating the resilience and transcendence of the human spirit in the face of adversity.

points.title: 最后岁月
points.description: 贝多芬的最后四年是他创作生涯的巅峰，也是他最伟大的作品诞生的时期。1824年，他完成了《第九交响曲（合唱）》，这部作品首次将人声引入交响乐，成为音乐史上的里程碑。同年，他在维也纳首次公开演出这部作品，尽管已经完全失聪，但仍然坚持指挥。1825年，他创作了《庄严弥撒》的最终版本。1826年，他在侄子卡尔自杀未遂后遭受沉重打击，健康状况急剧恶化。1827年3月26日，贝多芬在维也纳去世，享年56岁。他的葬礼吸引了数万人参加，成为维也纳历史上最盛大的葬礼之一。贝多芬的去世标志着古典音乐时代的结束，他的音乐遗产影响了后世无数作曲家，成为人类文化遗产中最珍贵的部分之一。
points.descriptionEn: Beethoven's final four years represented the pinnacle of his creative career and the birth of his greatest works. In 1824, he completed his 'Ninth Symphony (Choral),' which introduced human voices into the symphony for the first time, becoming a milestone in music history. That same year, he conducted its premiere in Vienna, despite being completely deaf. In 1825, he completed the final version of the 'Missa Solemnis.' In 1826, he suffered a severe blow after his nephew Karl's suicide attempt, and his health deteriorated rapidly. On March 26, 1827, Beethoven died in Vienna at the age of 56. His funeral was attended by tens of thousands, becoming one of the most magnificent funerals in Vienna's history. Beethoven's death marked the end of the classical music era, and his musical legacy influenced countless composers, becoming one of the most precious parts of humanity's cultural heritage.

supporter.zh: 贝多芬被尊为音乐史上最伟大的作曲家之一，他的作品代表了人类精神力量的最高体现。支持者认为，贝多芬通过音乐克服了身体上的残疾，特别是失聪这一音乐家的致命打击，展现了人类意志的非凡力量。他的九部交响曲，尤其是《第九交响曲》，被认为是人类艺术成就的巅峰。贝多芬的音乐从古典主义到浪漫主义的转变，为后世音乐发展开辟了道路，影响了整个19世纪及以后的音乐创作。他的作品不仅具有艺术价值，更承载着对自由、平等和博爱的追求，成为人类共同的精神财富。
supporter.en: Beethoven is revered as one of the greatest composers in music history, whose works represent the highest expression of human spiritual strength. Supporters believe that Beethoven overcame physical disabilities, particularly his deafness—a devastating blow for a musician—demonstrating extraordinary human willpower. His nine symphonies, especially the Ninth, are considered the pinnacle of human artistic achievement. Beethoven's transition from classicism to romanticism paved the way for future musical development, influencing composition throughout the 19th century and beyond. His works possess not only artistic value but also carry the pursuit of freedom, equality, and fraternity, becoming a common spiritual treasure for humanity.

critic.zh: 批评者指出贝多芬存在性格缺陷和个人生活中的问题。他脾气暴躁，人际关系紧张，多次与朋友和学生发生冲突。在音乐创作上，一些评论家认为他后期的作品过于复杂和情感化，偏离了古典主义的平衡与和谐。此外，贝多芬在侄子监护权争夺战中的表现也备受争议，显示出他性格中自私和控制欲强的一面。他的音乐也被批评为过于个人化，缺乏普遍性，有时被认为是为了自我表达而非为听众创作。这些批评者认为，贝多芬的传奇形象在一定程度上被后世浪漫化，掩盖了他作为普通人的人性弱点。
critic.en: Critics point out Beethoven's character flaws and personal life issues. He had a volatile temper, strained relationships, and frequently clashed with friends and students. Musically, some critics argue his later works were overly complex and emotional, deviating from the balance and harmony of classicism. Additionally, Beethoven's involvement in his nephew's custody battle is controversial, revealing selfish and controlling aspects of his personality. His music has also been criticized as overly personal, lacking universality, and sometimes seen as self-expression rather than composition for audiences. These critics suggest that Beethoven's legendary image has been romanticized by later generations, masking his human weaknesses as an ordinary person.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，贝多芬被定义为连接古典与浪漫主义时代的桥梁人物。他的音乐既保留了古典主义的结构和形式，又注入了强烈的个人情感和创新元素，开创了浪漫主义音乐的先河。贝多芬的形象超越了音乐领域，成为人类面对逆境不屈不挠精神的象征。他的《第九交响曲》中的《欢乐颂》被欧盟采用为盟歌，成为和平与团结的象征。在流行文化中，贝多芬的形象经常与'天才'、'抗争'和'超越'等概念联系在一起，成为激励无数人的文化符号。历史学界普遍认为，贝多芬的音乐不仅代表了个人天才，更反映了法国大革命后欧洲社会变革的时代精神。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Beethoven is defined as a transitional figure connecting the classical and romantic eras. His music preserved classical structure and form while injecting intense personal emotion and innovation, pioneering romantic music. Beethoven's image transcends music, becoming a symbol of human resilience in the face of adversity. The 'Ode to Joy' from his Ninth Symphony was adopted as the EU anthem, symbolizing peace and unity. In popular culture, Beethoven is often associated with concepts like 'genius,' 'resistance,' and 'transcendence,' becoming a cultural symbol that inspires countless people. Historiography generally views Beethoven's music as representing not only individual genius but also the spirit of European social transformation following the French Revolution.

self.zh: 我要扼住命运的咽喉，它绝不能使我完全屈服。
self.en: I will seize fate by the throat; it shall certainly not bend and crush me completely.

others.zh: 贝多芬的音乐是建筑在人类痛苦之上的欢乐殿堂。
others.en: Beethoven's music is a temple of joy built upon human suffering.
